title: Kenyan Chicken Wrap
community: Urban Kenya — café and takeaway culture
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Chicken Wrap — spiced grilled chicken, kachumbari, sliced avocado, and garlic mayo wrapped in a warm chapati or flour tortilla. The portable Nairobi lunch — combining the traditional chapati with modern wrap culture.
longDesc: The Kenyan chicken wrap is the natural meeting point between the chapati tradition and urban café culture. The chapati makes a superior wrap — thicker, more flavourful, and more structurally sound than a plain tortilla. Filled with spiced grilled chicken, fresh kachumbari, and avocado, it is the perfect portable Nairobi lunch.
ingredients: 2 chapatis (see KEN016) or large flour tortillas
steps: Season chicken with paprika, cumin, and salt. Grill until cooked through. Slice thinly.
Warm chapatis briefly in a dry pan.
Spread garlic mayo over each chapati.
Layer: lettuce, chicken strips, kachumbari, avocado.
Roll firmly, tucking in the sides.
chefTips: Warm the chapati before assembling — it is more pliable and less likely to crack.
Do not overfill — it becomes impossible to roll.
The chapati is what makes this Kenyan — use it instead of tortilla where possible.
cookingScience: Warming the chapati reactivates the gluten network, making it more flexible and elastic — this is why warm chapati rolls without cracking while a cold one splits.
sustainabilityTips: Chapati wraps avoid the need for commercially produced flour tortillas.
healthBenefits: Chapati provides more fibre than plain tortilla.
culturalNote: The Kenyan chicken wrap perfectly illustrates how Nairobi's café culture takes global food formats and transforms them with local ingredients into something distinctly and confidently Kenyan.
